sections.title: SEO Content Writing
sections.text: We start with search data to decide what's worth writing, then produce clear, human-written copy that an editor reviews before publishing, and we measure its impact on visibility and traffic.

items.label: Angle, questions, sources, call to action
Human copy that answers, with no filler
Language and subject-matter editing before publishing
Connecting the page to search and reading its impact

sections.title: Not all content serves the same goal
sections.text: A service page attracts people who want to buy; an article attracts people looking for an answer. We choose the type of content based on where the visitor is in their decision.

items.heading: Service pages
items.label: Copy that explains the service and its scope, removes hesitation and leads to an inquiry or order.

items.heading: Articles & guides
items.label: Answers to the questions that come before a decision, building trust and feeding your service pages.

items.heading: Category pages
items.label: Descriptions that explain what a category includes and help visitors filter and choose.

items.heading: Product pages
items.label: Enough information to buy: specs, uses and the differences between options.

items.heading: Comparison pages
items.label: A neutral look at the differences between alternatives, for people comparing before they order.

items.heading: Support content
items.label: Post-purchase answers that cut down on repeat questions.

sections.title: From research to a published, measured page

items.heading: Research & intent
items.text: We identify what customers search for and what competing pages cover.

items.heading: Brief
items.text: We define the angle, questions, sources and the action we want the reader to take.

items.heading: Writing
items.text: Direct, human-written copy that answers the question without filler.

items.heading: Review
items.text: Language and subject-matter editing, checked against the brief.

items.heading: Publish & measure
items.text: Structured publishing, then tracking visibility and traffic.

sections.title: Tools support the research; people make the calls
sections.text: We use search data and analysis tools to choose topics and angles. The writing and review are done by an editor who understands your business and knows what matters to the reader.

items.heading: What the tools do
items.text: Spot demand, analyze competitor coverage, prioritize topics.

items.heading: What the editor does
items.text: Choose the angle, craft the answer, fact-check and match your brand voice.

sections.eyebrow: Content impact in a real project
sections.heading: 12.9K organic clicks in 28 days
sections.text: A medical services website, compared with 825 clicks in the previous period, after improving its pages and content and connecting search traffic to the right path through the site.
sections.label: Source: Search Console

items.question: Is your content written with AI tools?
items.answer: Tools help with research and coverage analysis. The writing and review are done by an editor, and we never publish copy without human editing.

items.question: How many articles do we need per month?
items.answer: The number isn't the goal. We first work out what your priority pages need, and improving existing pages can be more effective than adding new articles.

items.question: Do you write service pages, or only articles?
items.answer: We write both: service, category and product pages, as well as the articles and guides people read before making a decision.

items.question: How do you measure the success of SEO content?
items.answer: We track impressions and clicks in Search Console, and traffic and conversions in GA4, for every page.

items.question: Do you update old content?
items.answer: Yes. Updating a page that's losing visibility often pays off faster than creating a new one.

items.question: Can you write in our brand voice?
items.answer: We agree on tone and terminology at the start, and apply them to every piece before it's published.
